title: Performance prediction equation for the Valencia Marathon based on time and pacing in the half marathon
authors: Oficial-Casado F, Priego-Quesada JI, Perez-Soriano P
population: Runners who finished both the Valencia Half Marathon and Marathon in the same year (2022 and 2023) and ran the half faster than the marathon
findings: Three linear regressions were built: half-marathon time plus sex; plus age category; plus half-marathon pace range (max minus min relative speed).
Adding pace range did not improve prediction; the selected model had explained variance of 85% and a mean absolute error of 5.9%.
The overall accuracy of the obtained model was similar to Daniels' VDOT, but the two models behaved differently depending on runner performance level.
limitations: One city, two editions; only runners who ran the half faster than the marathon (selection); the abstract gives neither VDOT's own error nor the level-dependent pattern, and does not say whether age category helped; MAE of 5.9% is about 13-14 min for a 3:50 marathon.
implications: Treat half-to-marathon equivalence (regression or VDOT-style) as carrying about 6% mean absolute error in a large recreational sample; show a range, not a point.
Include sex in half-to-marathon regression; in-race pace range added nothing. The abstract does not establish a benefit of age category.
Check VDOT-style predictions separately by ability tier when calibrating, because the models diverged by level.

verification.notes: Crossref gives issued 2026-02-02 with a 2025 DOI prefix (EPMC pubYear 2025); year 2026 kept. Rewrote the implications: the abstract does not state a VDOT-specific MAE nor reject age category.
